AptSpec.description:
The object form of `apt`: a package list, a file listing packages, or both.
A bare list of names folds into `packages`.

file.description: Path to a package-list file to install from, one name per line.

BrewSpec.description:
The object form of `brew`: taps, formulae and casks, or a Brewfile. A bare
list of names folds into `formulae`.

file.description:
Path to a Brewfile to apply instead of (or alongside) `taps`,
`formulae` and `casks`.

taps.description: Third-party taps to add before installing formulae/casks.

CargoSpec.description:
The object form of `cargo`: crates to install, a `Cargo.toml` to install
from, or both. A bare list of names folds into `packages`.

file.description: Path to a `Cargo.toml` whose binaries to install instead of `packages`.

ConfigSourceMetadata.description: `metadata`: identifying information for a config source.

description.description: A one-line human summary of what this source provides.

name.description:
The source's published name, as its maintainer spells it. Shown wherever
the manifest is displayed (`cfgd source show`, the summary a subscriber
approves before trusting the source) and carried in `-o json` output.
Required. A subscriber registers the source under a local name of their
own choosing, so this value identifies the source to a reader rather
than keying anything cfgd stores.

version.description: The source manifest's own version, shown to subscribers.

ConfigSourcePolicy.description:
`spec.policy`: the four acceptance tiers a config source offers items
under, plus the constraints it enforces on every subscriber.

```yaml
policy:
  required:
    packages:
      apt: [git]
  recommended:
    modules: [nvim]
  optional:
    modules: [tmux]
  locked:
    env:
      - name: COMPANY_PROXY
        value: http://proxy.internal:3128
  constraints:
    noScripts: true
```

constraints.description: Restrictions this source imposes on how subscribers may compose it.

locked.description: Items every subscriber receives and cannot override locally.

optional.description: Items a subscriber must explicitly name in `subscription.optIn` to receive.

recommended.description: Items a subscriber receives when `subscription.acceptRecommended` is set.

ConfigSourceProfileEntry.description:
Detailed profile entry in a ConfigSource manifest.
When present, provides richer info than the flat `profiles` list.

description.description: A one-line human summary of the profile.

inherits.description: Names of other published profiles this one inherits from.

name.description:
Name the profile is published under, and the value `cfgd profile
switch` takes to activate it.

path.description:
Path to the profile's manifest within the source repository, if not at
the conventional location.

ConfigSourceProvides.description: `spec.provides`: what a config source makes available to subscribers.

modules.description: Names of modules this source publishes.

platformProfiles.description:
Maps a platform/distro tag (`macos`, `debian`, …) to the profile name
to use on that platform.

profileDetails.description:
Published profiles with descriptions, paths, and inheritance — richer
than the flat `profiles` list.

profiles.description:
Flat list of published profile names. Superseded by `profileDetails`
when that list is non-empty.

ConfigSourceSpec.description: `spec`: the body of a config source manifest.

policy.description:
Policy tiers (required/recommended/optional/locked) and constraints
this source enforces on subscribers.

provides.description: Profiles and modules this source publishes.

CustomManagerSpec.description:
A user-defined package manager under `spec.packages.custom[]`, driven
entirely by shell commands.

```yaml
custom:
  - name: asdf
    check: "command -v asdf"
    listInstalled: "asdf list"
    install: "asdf install {package}"
    uninstall: "asdf uninstall {package}"
    packages: [nodejs]
```

check.description: Command that exits zero when this manager is available on the machine.

install.description: Command template to install a package; `{package}` is substituted.

listInstalled.description: Command whose stdout lists installed package names, one per line.

name.description: Manager name, used in `prefer:`/`deny:` lists and status output.

packages.description: Package names to install with this manager.

uninstall.description: Command template to uninstall a package; `{package}` is substituted.

update.description: Command to refresh the manager's own package index/cache before installs.

EncryptionConstraint.description: Encryption constraint applied to files from a config source.

backend.description: If set, restrict which backend is acceptable.

mode.description: If set, restrict which encryption mode is acceptable.

requiredTargets.description: Glob patterns or explicit paths that must be encrypted.

EncryptionMode.description: Controls when encryption is required for a managed file.

oneOf.description: File must be encrypted when stored in the repository.
File must always be encrypted, including at rest on disk.

EncryptionSpec.description: Encryption settings for a managed file.

mode.description: When encryption must be enforced. Defaults to `InRepo`.

name.description: Variable name. Must be shell-safe and not a reserved `CFGD_*` name.

platforms.description:
Platform tags gating this entry alone. Empty means every platform the
declaring module or profile is not already gated off of. Tags are
matched against the machine's OS, distro, and arch; use `macos` for
macOS. An entry gated off this host is not part of its desired state at
all: it appears on no surface, exactly as a platform-filtered package
does.

value.description:
Value assigned to the variable, exported verbatim into the shell
environment.

oneOf.description: Create a symbolic link from target to source (default).
Render a Tera template and write the output (auto-selected for .tera files).
Create a hard link from target to source.

Merge structured keys/values into the target, or pipe it through a
script, leaving everything else untouched. Requires a `patch:` block.

FlatpakSpec.description:
The object form of `flatpak`: application ids and the remote to install
them from. A bare list of ids folds into `packages`.

remote.description:
Remote to install from (e.g. `flathub`). Falls back to Flatpak's
configured default remote when omitted.

ManagedFileSpec.description:
One entry of `spec.files.managed[]`: a file this profile deploys.

```yaml
files:
  managed:
    - source: files/gitconfig
      target: ~/.gitconfig
      permissions: "644"
```

patch.description:
Structured merge or script configuration for `strategy: Patch`.
Required when `strategy` is `Patch`, rejected otherwise.

permissions.description: Unix permission bits (e.g. "600", "644") to apply after deployment.

private.description:
When true, the source file is local-only: auto-added to .gitignore,
silently skipped on machines where it doesn't exist.

source.description:
Path to the source file. Not required when `strategy` is `Patch`;
required otherwise.

strategy.description:
Per-file deployment strategy override. Omitted, the profile-wide
default applies.

target.description:
Destination path on the machine. A leading `~` expands to the home
directory.

NpmSpec.description:
The object form of `npm`: global packages, a `package.json` to install
from, or both. A bare list of names folds into `global`.

file.description: Path to a `package.json` to install dependencies from.

global.description: Package names to install globally (`npm install -g`).

PackageListSpec.description:
The map form of a bare-list manager (`pipx`, `dnf`, `apk`, …): the same
list under a `packages` key.

PackagesSpec.description:
`spec.packages`: packages to install, grouped by package manager.

Every manager field accepts either a bare list of names or (for the
managers with options of their own) a mapping:

```yaml
packages:
  brew:
    formulae: [ripgrep, fzf]
    casks: [alacritty]
  apt: [curl, git]
  cargo: [ripgrep]
```

PatchFormat.description: File format used to interpret and re-serialize a `Patch`-strategy target.

oneOf.description: INI sections/keys, edited line-by-line to preserve comments and layout.
JSON, re-serialized on write (no comments to preserve).
YAML; comments are NOT preserved across a merge (see docs for the caveat).
TOML, edited in place to preserve comments and layout.

PatchSpec.description:
Configuration for the `Patch` file strategy: a structured merge (`ensure`)
or a content-rewriting script, applied on top of the target's current
content.

ensure.description:
Keys/values to deep-merge into the target, leaving unmentioned keys
untouched. Values are literal (no template rendering). Mutually
exclusive with `script`.

format.description:
File format to parse the target as. Inferred from the target's
extension when omitted.

script.description:
A script path or an inline command that receives the target's current
content on stdin and writes the new content to stdout. A relative path
resolves against the module directory for a module file
(`spec.files[]`) and against the config directory for a profile file
(`spec.files.managed[]`); a value that resolves to no file is run as an
inline command. Mutually exclusive with `ensure`.

PolicyItems.description:
The content a config source offers under one policy tier
(`required`/`recommended`/`optional`/`locked`).

aliases.description: Shell aliases offered at this tier.

env.description: Environment variables offered at this tier.

modules.description: Module names offered at this tier.

profiles.description: Profile names this tier recommends composing in.

system.description: System configurator settings offered at this tier.

SecretSpec.description:
One entry of `spec.secrets[]`: a secret resolved into a file, into
environment variables, or both. At least one of `target` / `envs` must be
set; an entry carrying both writes the file AND exports the variables from
one resolution.

```yaml
secrets:
  - source: op://Personal/GitHub/token
    envs: [GITHUB_TOKEN]
  - source: ssh_key
    target: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  - source: vault://secret/data/api#key
    target: ~/.config/api-key
    envs: [API_KEY]
```

backend.description:
Secret backend name to resolve `source` with. Falls back to
`spec.secrets.backend` from `cfgd.yaml` when omitted.

envs.description:
Environment variable names to export the decrypted value under. May be
combined with `target`.

source.description:
Backend-specific reference to the secret (a 1Password `op://` URI, a
Vault path, a sops-encrypted file key, …).

target.description: File path to write the decrypted secret to. May be combined with `envs`.

template.description:
Template rendered around the resolved value before it is written to
`target` or exported under `envs`: every `${secret:value}` in it is
replaced by the value (`template: "token: ${secret:value}"`). Only a
provider reference (`op://`, `vault://`, …) resolves to a single value,
so `template` is rejected on a sops-encrypted file source.

command.description:
Command the alias expands to, written in the syntax of the shell it is
generated for. It may carry arguments, pipes and quotes: cfgd quotes the
whole value per dialect when it writes the alias definition, so the text
reaches the shell exactly as declared. Required — an alias with no
command has nothing to expand to.

name.description: Alias name, as typed at the shell prompt.

platforms.description:
Platform tags gating this entry alone. Empty means every platform the
declaring module or profile is not already gated off of. Tags are
matched against the machine's OS, distro, and arch; use `macos` for
macOS. An entry gated off this host is not part of its desired state at
all: it appears on no surface, exactly as a platform-filtered package
does.

SnapSpec.description:
The object form of `snap`: strict and classic-confinement snaps. A bare
list of names folds into `packages`.

packages.description: Snap names installed with default (strict) confinement.

SourceConstraints.description:
`spec.policy.constraints`: restrictions a config source imposes on every
subscriber, independent of which tier delivered an item.

allowSystemChanges.description: Allow this source to deliver `system:` configurator settings. Default: `false`.

allowedTargetPaths.description:
Glob patterns restricting which file targets this source may deploy to.
Empty means no restriction.

encryption.description: Encryption requirements imposed on files delivered by this source.

noScripts.description:
Reject lifecycle scripts (profile-layer and module `run:` bodies) this
source delivers, unless a subscriber opts in via
`subscription.allowScripts`. Default: `true`.

noSecretsRead.description:
Reject `${secret:…}` references this source's delivered content
resolves. Default: `true`.

requireSignedCommits.description:
Require that the HEAD commit in this source's git repo has a valid
GPG or SSH signature. ORed with the subscriber's
`subscription.requireSignedCommits`, so either side asking is enough.
Subscribers can bypass both with `spec.security.allowUnsigned`.
